label: nxd-review-closure: adversarial review round over an authored closure
notes: NO MEASURABLE CORRECTNESS EFFECT at N=1 per arm; recorded as such rather than as a win. All three runs scored 16/17 on treasury-yield-curve. The only check that moved, tier2-measure-reconciliation, went FAIL -> PASS -> FAIL across control, reviewed-run1 and reviewed-run2 (identical skill-set, prompt and scenario for the two reviewed runs), so it is unstable rather than responsive to the review round; an earlier reading of run1 alone as a win was withdrawn. What the runs do support: no correctness regression, and no efficiency regression - the reviewed runs used FEWER main-thread turns and tokens than the control (31-34 vs 35 turns, ~3% fewer output tokens, 5-9% cheaper), so dispatching the review subagent did not add turns to the orchestrator. The anti-signal this experiment was designed to catch - the reviewed arm scoring worse because the builder accepted fabricated critique instead of adjudicating it - did not appear. The scenario had only one check of headroom (control 16/17) because a prompt-extraction fix in this same PR raised the control from an earlier ~14/17, so this instrument could not have shown a large effect; N>=5 per arm, or a scenario with more semantic headroom, is needed for a real verdict. Runtime caveat: reviewed-run1's determinism cell failed for environmental reasons (the installed supervisor baked NXD_DESKTOP_REPO_ROOT to a deleted worktree); control ran on supervisor db0e8ab3a / wheels 0.41.143 and reviewed-run2 on 173737f6c / 0.41.144 after rebuilding from main, which is itself a confounder between those two cells.

checks.why: The agent read all five files, explicitly identified that 2020–2021 lack the `4 Mo` column while 2022–2024 have it, verified dlt's union behavior empirically, and read raw headers per file with stdlib csv — confirmed by the landed data showing 2020-06-15 with exactly the 12 correct labels (no `4 Mo`, `30 Yr` present, no positional misalignment).

`yield_curve_daily` lands 15,562 rows with `maturity_label` as a column value at (obs_date x maturity) grain, queried in the read-back as `select maturity_label, maturity_months, yield_pct ... order by maturity_months`.
The tenor_bucket distribution (bill=6805 vs note=6255=5x1251) implies exactly 550 non-null `4 Mo` observations, so the 199 blank 2022 cells produced no fabricated 0.00% rows.

Landed count is exactly 15,562 (not the dense 16,263), `4 Mo` totals 550 non-null observations, and the 2020-06-15 spot check shows `4 Mo` absent while `30 Yr` is present — the per-maturity-per-year distribution, not just the aggregate, is right.

The derived rows carry `maturity_months` and `tenor_bucket` — the latter serves no arithmetic purpose and exists only in maturities.csv, showing the reference table is read and joined rather than a label→months literal, and the read-back orders the curve by the numeric `maturity_months`.

`maturities` lands 1:1 from the pristine CSV (the agent's dlt probe confirmed all four columns — maturity_label, maturity_months, tenor_bucket, first_published — land), and the Q4 read-back answers bills/notes/bonds from `tenor_bucket` (6/5/2).

The monthly Q3 figures are averages (2020-01 = 1.7576 for 10 Yr, not a sum), no Agg.SUM over yield appears anywhere, and the mean choice is explicitly stated in the handoff and landed as the `monthly_yield_aggregation` decision row.
`curve_spread_daily` lands 1,251 rows — one per observation date — carrying `spread_pct`, `curve_shape`/inversion, and the endpoint labels, a genuine regrain keyed on date.

The ruling is landed as queryable data (the `curve_spread_endpoints` row in the landed `nxd_decisions` model, verified by SQL read-back, plus per-row `short_maturity_label`/`long_maturity_label` columns) and the handoff states the definition used (day's extreme published maturities, 1 Mo/30 Yr, 511 inverted days) — the decision is not silent.

The transform dry-run printed grain-derived counts for every model (yield_curve_daily 15,562; curve_spread_daily 1,251 reconciling to the 1,251 distinct source dates) and the agent states the asserts compare landed rows against an independent re-read of the source CSVs.

Nothing in the trace or final answer shows a signed yield-total reconciliation for the measure-bearing `yield_curve_daily` model, nor an itemized named exclusion term for the 199 blank `4 Mo` cells required by the non-null-only shape it landed — only a generic 'reconciliation asserts' claim.

The agent explicitly reads source headers/rows with stdlib `csv` for the derived unpivot, follows the template's single `pipeline.run` with resources appended, and no pandas/pyarrow or nested values appear (the read-back shows only the five expected flat tables, no `parent__field` children).

No wall-clock, random, or model/network call appears anywhere in the trace's transform description; dates land as ISO from the MM/DD/YYYY source via an explicit parse, and the inversion ruling was decided agent-side and landed as data before the build.
The authoritative runner fact reports {"exit_code": 0, "failures": [], "passed": true}, matching the trace's 8/8 PASS with rows identical across all five tables.

The final `find` shows exactly CONTEXT.md, csv-source-path, data/*, infra-profile.yaml, models.py, requirements.txt, spec.py, transform/main.py — no hand-written deployment-spec.yaml, manifest.yaml, or models.yaml (those exist only under the supervisor-generated definitions snapshot).

BASE_MODELS (treasury_par_yields, maturities, nxd_decisions) each have a data/ directory and the two derived models (yield_curve_daily, curve_spread_daily) have none, and all five names read back consistently from the landed DuckDB, so PHYSICAL_MODELS covers the derived models too.

Sources were copied with `cp -p` and md5 comparison of source vs copy matched, no file was re-headered or padded (the 2022 file keeps its 199 blank `4 Mo` cells and 2020/2021 keep 12 maturity columns), and reshaping happens only in the derived unpivot.

verdict.summary: A near-exemplary run — correct drift-tolerant unpivot (15,562 rows, 550 non-null `4 Mo`), landed decisions ledger, deterministic double build — but the Tier-2 measure reconciliation with a named exclusion term for the 199 blank cells is never demonstrated in the transcript.

verdict.summary: A strong run that handles the schema drift, blank-cell, fabrication, ordering, semi-additivity, disclosure, and determinism traps correctly, but the transcript provides no evidence of the required Tier-2 measure reconciliation with an itemized exclusion term for the 199 blank `4 Mo` cells.
